analysis.title: Global Rates Trader: Moving Deliberately
key_insights: Central bank decisions last week signaled a deliberate approach to further tightening. Risk asset volatility, not policy, is the main driver of global duration. AI-related volatility has replaced energy prices as the driver of directional yield moves (10y UST yield correlation with AI-related equities versus Brent).

The shift from energy risk to AI worries has re-coupled longer-term US forwards with GS fair value. GS estimates still show real money underweight duration, so the rally has room to extend if risk asset volatility persists.

US: the GS economists' baseline is one more Fed hike in December, with an every-other-meeting pattern. A third hike in March is a risk if inflation surprises up. Chair Warsh said the Fed will devote one meeting next year and two in 2028 to broad policy strategy. The curve steepened on that, which GS reads as a dovish interpretation of the schedule change.

Trade change: GS closes the receive 10y on the 5s10s30s SOFR fly (+3bp) and adds a long 5s position on the 2s5s30s UST fly (entry -44bp, target -60bp, stop -35bp). The reasons are lower very front-end hike risk, 5s tending to outperform during and just after hiking cycles, and skewed long-end risks at the refunding.

Treasury refunding next week: GS expects unchanged 10-to-30y coupon auction sizes and steady or modestly higher buyback envelopes. A cut in long-end sizes is a risk but not the base case. GS expects Treasury to signal possible auction size changes and to begin raising 2-to-7y sizes in May 2027. Market expectations lean toward cuts, so unchanged sizes could disappoint and push long-end spreads wider.

Front-end pressure in the US is in T-bills, which have cheapened versus OIS since late August. GS cites elevated bill supply, money funds shortening maturity, and flat money fund AUM since summer. Long-term bond funds have had healthy inflows, which has smoothed duration digestion.

Canada: the BoC hiked 25bp as expected with a more hawkish tone, but guided that policy will proceed carefully. Markets price 13bp of hikes by year-end and about 100bp through end-2027. GS calls the CAD front-end hike premium excessive because trim and median inflation are below 2%, AI volatility has cut hike pricing at peers, and an upside surprise would mostly pull hikes forward. GS recommends CAD front-end flatteners.

Euro area: the ECB communication set a high bar against not hiking in December, so GS expects the market to decay toward fully pricing it. The restrained tone on sovereign spreads should dampen volatility. With rates volatility elevated versus fair value, GS sees risks skewed toward 5y outperformance on the EUR curve. EU bonds look fair against Euro area fundamentals, and GS sees EU outperformance versus peers in 2027 as NGEU issuance ends and EU supply roughly halves to EUR 70bn.

UK: GS economists expect the BoE to hike next week and once more in February. With tightening largely priced, GS sees a high bar for more front-end cheapening, with energy escalation the main risk. The GBP-EUR front-end vol differential is compressed relative to the rate differential, so GS favors long GBP versus EUR front-end vol, for example owning front-end GBP receivers versus EUR.

UK Budget matched expectations. The deficit path rose by GBP 13bn a year on average, headroom fell to GBP 15bn, and the gilt remit rose only GBP 4bn with the long-term share cut from about 10% to 6%. GS prefers Gilts versus swaps and expects modest further long-end swap spread widening. It expects 10y UK to underperform peers because fiscal challenges are deferred, not resolved, and prefers expressing the supply improvement through asset swaps.

Japan: GS economists moved their expected BoJ hike to December on Ueda's focus on price upside risks, yen weakness if the Fed hikes, and easing fiscal concerns. Safe-haven demand tied to AI wobbles has driven JGB curve moves. Continued AI concerns would support JGB richening, long-end outperformance and bull flattening.

Antipodes: the RBNZ held the OCR in a surprise 4-3 vote while guiding toward further hikes. GS economists now expect hikes in December and March, below market pricing. GS recommends 2s10s NZD steepeners (entry 61bp, target 75bp, stop 54bp) because NZD term premium is the lowest among peers. In Australia, GS expects a final RBA hike next week and keeps front-end flattening exposure such as 2s5s, but closes the IRZ6U7 flattener for about 25bp.

macro_indicators.reading: One more hike in December as baseline, risk of a third hike in March if inflation surprises up, every-other-meeting approach
macro_indicators.interpretation: Hike risk at the very front end of the US curve has fallen, which supports rotating into 5s.
Tone on inflation and growth was more hawkish, but guidance to proceed carefully means a December hike is not the baseline.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS considers this cumulative pricing excessive and vulnerable to a pullback, and favors CAD front-end flattening.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Surprise hold with guidance toward further hikes. It lowers near-term hike expectations and supports 2s10s NZD steepening.

macro_indicators.reading: 3.15% (September projection, which GS says could be exceeded)
macro_indicators.interpretation: The bank guided toward hikes that could exceed this trajectory.

macro_indicators.reading: Two hikes, in December and March
macro_indicators.interpretation: Below market pricing in both pace and magnitude.

macro_indicators.reading: December hike on track, high bar not to hike
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market should decay toward fully pricing the December meeting absent major developments.

macro_indicators.reading: First hike of the cycle next week, one further hike in February
macro_indicators.interpretation: Substantial tightening is already priced, so the bar for more front-end cheapening is high.
A weaker yen risk after a December Fed hike would push the BoJ to hike.

macro_indicators.reading: Hike next week, expected to be the final one of the cycle
macro_indicators.interpretation: Firmer underlying inflation supports the hike. GS closed its AUD IRZ6U7 flattener on unclear asymmetry around the meeting.

macro_indicators.reading: Revised GBP 13bn higher per year on average, fiscal headroom GBP 15bn
macro_indicators.interpretation: Largely reflects higher interest costs. The Budget cleared a near-term hurdle but left fiscal challenges unresolved.
Issuance was revised higher for 2027/28 and 2028/29 versus March, supporting 10y underperformance on the UK curve.
NGEU-related issuance ends in 2026, which supports EU bond outperformance versus peers in 2027.
GS forecasts 10y yields below spot and below forwards across the horizon.

trade_ideas.description: Long 5s on the 2s5s30s UST fly. Entry -44bp, target -60bp, stop -35bp.
trade_ideas.rationale: Less very front-end hike risk, 5s tend to outperform during and right after hiking cycles, and long-end risks are skewed at next week's refunding.
trade_ideas.risk: Further hawkish Fed repricing or a sharp reversal in risk asset volatility.

trade_ideas.description: CAD front-end flatteners, 1y1y vs 1y or CORH7Z7. Entry 40bp, target 25bp, stop 50bp.
trade_ideas.rationale: Cumulative BoC hike premium is excessive given sub-2% trim and median inflation, AI volatility weighing on peers' hike pricing, and upside data mostly pulling hikes forward.
trade_ideas.risk: A December BoC hike if inflation data surprise up meaningfully or a trade deal is reached.

trade_ideas.rationale: RBNZ hold lowers near-term hike expectations, while uncertainty and above-target inflation sustain term premium further out. NZD term premium is the lowest among peers and carry is favorable.

trade_ideas.description: AUD front-end flattening exposure such as 2s5s. The IRZ6U7 flattener is closed for potential profit of 25bp.
trade_ideas.rationale: Flattening can extend under either bullish global duration spillovers or renewed hawkish pressure on the RBA path.
trade_ideas.risk: Less clear asymmetry around next week's RBA meeting.

trade_ideas.description: Long GBP versus EUR front-end vol, for example owning front-end GBP receivers versus EUR.
trade_ideas.rationale: The GBP-EUR front-end vol differential is compressed relative to the rates differential and is expected to normalize, most likely on energy de-escalation.

trade_ideas.description: Long Gilts versus swaps, expressed through asset swaps rather than outright duration, with 10y UK underperformance versus peers.
trade_ideas.rationale: Reduced long-end issuance and reduced QT support Gilts versus swaps, while unresolved fiscal pressure argues for 10y underperformance.

trade_ideas.description: EUR curve 5y outperformance, with a flatter 2s5s curve on energy-driven front-end uncertainty.
trade_ideas.rationale: 5s on the broader curve tend to outperform in a more restrained vol environment, and ECB communication on sovereign spreads should be vol dampening.
trade_ideas.risk: Energy escalation and sovereign spread widening.

risk_factors: Energy escalation tied to the Iran conflict, which would hit UK front-end pricing hardest and could reopen hike risk in Europe.
AI-related risk asset volatility, the current main driver of yields, which could reverse the duration rally.
A downside surprise in next Friday's US labor market report, to which the market is prone to react strongly if risk tone stays weak.
Refunding disappointment: unchanged long-end auction sizes versus market expectations of cuts could cause long-end underperformance on the spread curve.
Sovereign spread widening and a possible French rating downgrade in the euro area.
Unresolved UK fiscal pressure, including a tight Spending Review next year and gross Gilt supply above GBP 300bn in 2027/28.
Possible Japanese fiscal news that has weighed on long-end JGBs before.
A December BoC hike if inflation surprises up or a trade deal is reached.
charts_described: Exhibit 1: AI-related volatility has taken the helm from energy prices as the driver of directional yield moves, showing 1-month correlations of the 10y UST yield with Brent and with AI-related equities from Oct-25 to Oct-26.
Exhibit 2: Money market fund AUM growth has stalled since summer, plotting YTD growth in $tn for 2024, 2025 and 2026.
Exhibit 4: 5s ought to outperform on the EUR curve in a more restrained vol environment, plotting EUR 3m5y implied vol against the EUR 2s5s30s fly.
Exhibit 6: GBP-EUR front-end vol has diverged from the relative rate differential, plotting 1y1y implied rate vol differential fitted on the 1y1y OIS differential.
Exhibit 7: Gilt issuance revised higher for 2027/28 and 2028/29, comparing October projected gross Gilt issuance with the March 2026 OBR forecast.
vol_and_positioning: AI-related volatility has subordinated energy volatility as the driver of yields. If the weaker risk tone persists, GS expects a stronger market reaction to a downside surprise in next Friday's labor market report.
GS estimates real money remains underweight duration even as longer-term bond funds see healthy inflows.

EUR rates volatility is elevated versus the GS fair value model and TTF prices are close to the commodities strategists' upside scenario. GS links 5s outperformance on the EUR curve to a more restrained vol environment.

The GBP-EUR front-end vol differential has compressed well below what the rates differential implies, partly due to elevated EUR vol amid sovereign uncertainty. GS sees relative value long GBP versus EUR front-end vol.

CFTC duration-weighted net positions: speculators are net short in all seven listed contracts (SFR -74.5, TU -28.9, FV -44.4, TY -56.8, TN -12.6, US -12.4, WN -58.3 $mm/bp). Asset managers and others are net long in all of them. Dealers are net long SFR (+57.6) and net short the rest.
GS positioning indicators: US option implied position indicator score 0, US fund positioning indicator score -3, US data response indicator score -1.
geopolitical: Iran conflict and its energy effects remain a driver of rates, with energy escalation named as a clear risk for BoE front-end pricing.
Next week's US midterm elections: the initial rates impact likely depends on perceived implications for AI and subsequent developments in the Iran conflict.
Speculation about a potential French rating downgrade has raised the beta of OAT and BTP spreads and put sovereign spread risk in focus for the ECB.
A possible Canada-US trade deal is cited as a trigger that could bring a BoC hike forward to December.

tension_points.bull_case: GS base case is unchanged 10-to-30y coupon sizes with steady or higher buybacks and guidance toward future increases in 2-to-7y sizes. Long-end spreads are wide to fair value, so a size cut is unnecessary on liquidity or demand grounds.
tension_points.bear_case: Market expectations lean toward reduced long-end sizes, so unchanged sizes could disappoint and cause long-end underperformance on the spread curve. GS expects the impact to be contained.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A reduction in 10-to-30y auction sizes at next week's refunding announcement, which GS flags as a risk but not its base case.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price 13bp of hikes by year-end and about 100bp through end-2027 after a hawkish BoC. A December hike is possible on a large inflation upside surprise or a trade deal.
tension_points.bear_case: GS sees the hike premium as excessive. Trim and median inflation are below 2%, the MPR projects growth below potential, and AI volatility has cut hike pricing at peers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A December BoC hike driven by a meaningful upside inflation surprise or a trade deal, which GS economists see as a risk.

tension_points.bull_case: AI-driven risk volatility has replaced energy as the yield driver, US longer-term forwards are back near fair value, and real money is still underweight duration, so the rally can extend.
tension_points.bear_case: Central banks, including the Fed, are still tightening, and an energy escalation tied to the Iran conflict could return as the dominant driver.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Risk asset volatility fading, since the report ties the rally's extension to volatility persisting.

tension_points.theme: UK gilts supply versus fiscal risk
tension_points.bull_case: The Budget cleared a near-term hurdle, the remit rose only GBP 4bn with a smaller long-term share, and reduced QT and lower long-end issuance support Gilts versus swaps.
tension_points.bear_case: Fiscal pressure is deferred, not resolved. Next year's Spending Review faces a smaller buffer and gross issuance exceeds GBP 300bn in 2027/28, which favors 10y underperformance versus peers.
